original_findings.actual: Both validation calls consume _SealedArchive; redirect is refused, foreign directory contains only unchanged keep sentinel, service starts0, failure/retention persisted; all13 captured descriptors closed.
Both linked and same-byte replacement inode archive paths are rejected with archive identity drift, no installed payload and starts0; source identity is checked through actual owner handoff.
Session mismatch produces installed deployment ownership mismatch before starts; altered returned receipt preserved in evidence and original receipt file, differing owner session observed.

new_findings.trigger: After the real protected installer returns, immediately before save_receipt, rename the sandbox parent to another newly owned fixture path and create a plain replacement directory at the original sandbox pathname.
new_findings.expected: Protected deployment failure handling must not write to the replacement parent; original error and retention disposition must be recorded against the original owned evidence parent or fail closed without foreign writes.
new_findings.actual: save_receipt rejects protected directory identity drift and closes all 20 tracked descriptors; archive deletion is fenced and both services remain unstarted, but inherited _prepare then writes default-preparation-failure.json via self.directory into the replacement directory; no failure record is written into the detached original parent, and root_retained=false describes the vanished pathname although the owned root still exists under the relocated parent.
new_findings.evidence: raw/probes.stdout.log: INDEPENDENT_ASSERTION failure_receipt_replaced_parent and final failed assertion
new_findings.scope: Deterministic POSIX synthetic namespace replacement; no real hostile process or native runtime was exercised.
new_findings.why_not_accepted_relocated_inode_limit: The observed write is to a newly created replacement inode after the original parent moved, not a write through a pinned descriptor to the original relocated inode.
new_findings.remedy_obligation: Keep the final failure evidence write and retention identity within the same anchored owned-parent lifetime; root decides the authorized implementation seam, without altering legacy default semantics.
